name: access
title: Access and approvals
summary: What staff may do and how much they may approve: staff roles, the permission registry, role assignments, leads and backups per work area, approval limits per role, approval requests with a second reviewer, and cover while someone is away. Granting access never grants financial authority.
owns: Staff roles: Business Owner, the 17 management roles of plan ch. 2 (Official Store, Purchasing, Inventory, Warehouse, Order, Shipping, Returns, Platform Administrator, Catalog, Seller, Customer Support, Finance, Marketing, Advertising, Content, Trust and Risk, Reports Analyst), task roles (warehouse worker, finance staff, support agent) and custom roles
Permission registry: every staff permission declared by every enabled module, grouped by work area
Role permissions and role assignments (one person can hold several roles; a role is a responsibility, not a person)
Lead, ordered backups and escalation role for every role's work area, with coverage gaps
Approval action registry (payouts, refunds, holds, seller restrictions, price changes, publication overrides, adjustments…) declared by owning modules
Approval limits per role and action, set by the Business Owner, with effective dates; changes to limits always need Business Owner approval
Authority checks: allowed, approval required or not permitted, for a principal, action and amount
Approval requests: one or two approvals, nominated reviewer, return with comment, reject, cancel, expiry, reminders; nobody approves their own request
Away periods: who covers each role while a lead is away, and (with Business Owner approval) temporary delegation of approval authority
notOwns: Staff accounts, sign-in, 2-step verification, invitations links and account lock/disable: identity (access calls identity.inviteStaff and reacts to identity.account.disabled)
Seller member roles and seller permissions (owner-only payout changes, etc.): sellers
Executing the approved action (releasing the payout, sending the refund, suspending the seller): the module that requested the approval, on access.approval.decided
The action history itself: audit (access records every role, permission, limit and approval change there)
Work items, queues, deadlines and escalation timers: workqueues (it uses lead/backup resolution from here)
Delivering notices to approvers and backups: notifications

stateMachines.name: Approval request
stateMachines.notes: approve moves to partially_approved while approvals < requiredApprovals; approveFinal is the approval that completes it. Each approver must be eligible (a role whose limit covers the amount, or a second-reviewer role above the threshold, or authority delegated during an away period), must not be the requester, and must not have approved the same request already. resubmit clears earlier approvals. approved, rejected, cancelled and expired publish access.approval.decided; the requesting module then acts. Approved is not executed: e.g. a payout shows Paid only after the bank confirms.

stateMachines.name: Limit change
stateMachines.notes: Every limit change needs Business Owner approval (action access.limits.change). A change proposed by a Business Owner is approved on creation for other roles' limits; a Business Owner cannot approve a change to a role they hold themselves when another Business Owner exists. Platform Administrators can propose but never approve. apply runs at effectiveFrom (job access.apply-limit-changes) and closes the previous rows (effective_to).

stateMachines.name: Role assignment
stateMachines.notes: Assignments to invited staff wait for identity.invitation.accepted. Assigning a role that carries sensitive permissions, or assigning any role to yourself, creates pending_approval with a second reviewer (action access.roles.sensitive-grant). approve is guarded: it leads to active when the person has already accepted their invitation (an existing staff account), otherwise to pending_acceptance until identity.invitation.accepted. Disabling the account (identity.account.disabled) revokes all assignments.

stateMachines.name: Away period
stateMachines.notes: Periods with delegateApprovals start in pending_approval (Business Owner approves the delegation: granting access is not financial authority). start and end run from the job at from/to; end can also be called early. Coverage only re-routes work and notices; covering people use their own limits unless delegation was approved, and then never more than the away person's limits.

SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED.meaning: You cannot approve or reject your own request.

NOT_ELIGIBLE_APPROVER.meaning: Your roles' limits do not cover this action or amount. details.eligibleRoles lists who can.

ALREADY_APPROVED_BY_YOU.meaning: The second approval must come from a different person.

SYSTEM_ROLE.meaning: Seeded roles cannot be archived or have their key changed.

ROLE_IN_USE.meaning: Remove the role from all staff before archiving it.

LAST_BUSINESS_OWNER.meaning: At least one active Business Owner must remain.

COVERAGE_INVALID.meaning: Lead and backups must hold the role, a backup cannot be the lead, and every led role needs cover. details.issues.

AWAY_OVERLAP.meaning: This person already has an away period in that time.

UNKNOWN_PERMISSION.meaning: details.keys are not in the permission registry (or their module is disabled).

UNKNOWN_APPROVAL_ACTION.meaning: The action key is not registered by any enabled module.

REMINDER_TOO_SOON.meaning: Reviewers were reminded recently; try again after details.nextAllowedAt.

notes: Granting access is not financial authority. Permissions decide which screens and actions a person can open; approval limits decide how much they may approve. A permission such as finance.payouts.approve is necessary but never sufficient: check() also needs a limit covering the amount. Platform Administrators (access.roles.manage) can grant permissions but cannot set or approve limits, and cannot approve their own requests.

Approval actions are declared by the owning module in its spec and manifest (`approvalActions`: key, desc, limit money|units|percent|none, secondReviewer always|above-limit|never, approvers; see FORMAT.md), next to its permissions, and registered at boot. Every endpoint `approval` rule names its action key. Declared actions include finance.payouts.release, finance.holds.place / finance.holds.release, finance.adjustments.record, returns.refunds.approve, sellers.sellers.restrict / sellers.sellers.suspend (always second reviewer) / sellers.sellers.close, offers.prices.change (percent), inventory.adjustments.apply (units), purchasing.orders.send, shipping.claims.open, support.remedies.approve, wallet.goodwill.grant, promotions.budgets.approve, advertising.rules.change, customers.accounts.close-with-obligations, trust.enforcements.reverse and settings.changes.apply. access declares access.limits.change, access.roles.sensitive-grant and access.delegations.approve. A catalog publication override action (catalog.products.publication-override) is not declared yet; catalog is owned by the lead.

Second reviewer logic: if the requester's own limit covers the amount but it is above the second-review threshold, the request starts with requesterCountsAsFirst = true and needs one more approver from secondReviewerRoleKeys. If the amount is above the requester's limit, it needs approvers whose limits cover it (and a second one above their threshold). Actions declared with secondReviewer = always need one approver other than the requester whatever the amount.

Modules follow one pattern: call check(); if allowed, act; if approval_required, call requestApproval(), keep their record pending, return 202 or APPROVAL_REQUIRED with details.approvalRequestId, and finish on access.approval.decided (approved: execute; rejected/cancelled/expired: revert the pending record). They embed approvalInfo() in their responses so screens can show who must approve.

Lead and backups: notices and work for a role go to its lead; while the lead is away (or locked) they go to the first available backup and the lead sees them on return. notifications and workqueues use resolveRecipients(); routing changes are announced with access.coverage.changed.

Seeded system roles (keys): business_owner, platform_administrator, official_store_manager, purchasing_manager, inventory_manager, warehouse_manager, order_manager, shipping_manager, returns_manager, catalog_manager, seller_manager, customer_support_manager, finance_manager, marketing_manager, advertising_manager, content_manager, trust_and_risk_manager, reports_analyst, plus task roles warehouse_worker, finance_staff, support_agent. Seeded limits are example values from the prototype and must be confirmed by the Business Owner.
Every write here is recorded through audit.record with before/after (permission sets, limit values, coverage) and the approval request id.
